factors.name: Size and parallel/choice branching
factors.summary: Very high loadings (0.90–0.97) of Token split, Number of empty sequence flows, Control flow complexity, Size and Coefficient of network connectivity show that larger nets in this dataset also have more splits, more parallel branches and more arcs per node. Maximum connector degree (0.76, with 0.39 on Factor 2) and Connector Mismatch (0.55, communality only 0.35) join more moderately. Density loads -0.46 here, consistent with larger nets being sparser.

factors.name: Connector degree and density
factors.summary: Average connector degree (0.89) and Density (0.84) load highly, so nets with high-degree connectors also tend to be dense, independent of size. Connector Heterogeneity loads negatively (-0.58, communality 0.35), so such nets tend to have less mixed connector types. Density also has a secondary loading of -0.46 on Factor 1.

factors.name: Sequentiality / structural simplicity
factors.summary: Sequentiality (0.96) and Separability (0.69) define this factor, so nets with many arcs between non-connector nodes also have many articulation points, i.e. chain-like, decomposable structure. The factor rests on only two measures, and the Sequentiality loading is affected by a possible Heywood case.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO is 0.83, with every per-measure MSA above 0.6. The three varimax factors match the three eigenvalues above 1 and explain 82% of the variance. Factor 1 (49%) is a dominant size and branching dimension. Factor 2 (17%) captures connector degree and density, and Factor 3 (16%) captures sequential, separable structure. All measures are assigned and no cross-loadings were flagged by the 0.15 gap rule, although Maximum connector degree and Density have notable secondary loadings.
caveats: The communality of Sequentiality is about 1.02, a possible Heywood case, so its loading and Factor 3 should be read with care.
Connector Mismatch and Connector Heterogeneity have low communalities (about 0.35) and are only weakly represented by the solution.
Connector Heterogeneity is undefined for nets without connectors, which may affect its correlations depending on how missing values were handled.
Number of duplicate tasks was removed as constant, so duplication is not represented in these factors.
The factors reflect shared variance in these 288 discovered nets and depend on the discovery algorithms, the rotation and the chosen number of factors.
